mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an active monetary easing cycle that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point monthly rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp monthly, or Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal a sharp contraction in consumer demand that depresses corporate earnings expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing slowdown (INDPRO < 90.0) indicates weakening supply chain activity that pressures corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days during economic deceleration.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 90.0, or Rank IC over 3 years < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) signals robust economic growth that supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 grows, or Rank IC over 3 years < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% (CPIAUCSL) triggers hawkish monetary policy expectations that raise bond yields and depress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending, driving negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high interest rate environments (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), elevated borrowing costs reduce corporate profitability, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days during monetary tightening cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or Rank IC over 3 years < 0.03.
